title: Clifford the Big Red Dog
overview: Clifford the Big Red Dog is a fun show aimed towards younger audiences. Clifford, a 20 foot tall red dog, plays with his dog friends, Cleo and T-Bone, and has great adventures with them. Clifford's best friend, however, is Emily Elizabeth Howard, his owner. Emily has friends of her own and all the characters live peacefully on Birdwell Island. Each Clifford the Big Red Dog episode consists of two stories, linked by a "Speckle Story," a story read to Clifford by Emily Elizabeth about the adventures of a dog named Speckle. At the end of each episode is a "big idea" presented by Clifford, followed by a short promotional spot for one of the characters on Clifford. Also included is a short segment featuring a real kid with his/her dog.

episodes.overview: A scene from the fourth episode of the first season of the 1964 Hanna-Barbera version of Clifford the Big Red Dog. Here, Betty Rubble (Bea Benaderet) reads Bamm Bamm (Don Messick) a story about chicken soup with rice. Interestingly enough, Betty Rubble reads the exact same words that were also used when the book was published. Credit goes to Jack for random background music. NOTE: It took a while to get Mel Blanc's Barney Rubble voice right, while recording the dialogue.

episodes.title: Clifford The Big Red Dog Season 6 Episode 7 Birdwell's Got Talent ( Fanmad Made With Clipchamp
episodes.overview: A scene from the 7th episode of the 6th season of the 2000 version of Clifford the Big Red Dog. Here in this scene, Tammy adds additional lyrics to an already familiar song that was sung all the way back to the second season. NOTE: Even though Kathryn Beaumont recorded some of the new lyrics for the tune in this season 6 episode, surprisingly enough, John Ritter still provided Clifford's singing voice for the song even though the episode aired in August 2006, almost 3 years after he passed away in 2003 This is because most of the lyrics in the song in this episode are recycled from the season 2 episode Doghouse Rock, which aired in February 2003 7 months before John Ritter passed away in September of that year. The season 6 episode itself has Harry Groener voice, when Clifford is NOT singing, except for 1 spoken line where John Ritter voiced him when Clifford says "Say Wow!" near the end of the song. The only lyrics that are brand new to this episode are sung/spoken by Tammy the green British poodle, played by Kathryn Beaumont,  but other than that, the rest of the song reuses audio from the season 2 episode Doghouse Rock.

episodes.title: Clifford The Big Red Dog Season 6 Episode 7 Birdwell's Got Talent (for HuskyDog88
episodes.overview: The most perfect version of the scene from the 7th episode of the 6th season of the 2000 version of Clifford the Big Red Dog, featuring the debut of Tammy the green British poodle, voiced by Kathryn Beaumont, and this marks Kathryn Beaumont's very first time she did major voicework of an animated character, after her last major voice role was 53 years earlier in 1953 when she voiced Wendy in Disney's Peter Pan. Yesterday, I worked extremely hard to get Kathryn Beaumont's voice on another ai website. It took 4 and a half minutes to record parts of her current voice, and then it took about 3 hours for the training of the voice to be completed. And the best part was, even though Play HT failed to match her British accent with her current voice, making the voice sound more American than it was British, Weights ai actually managed to get her correct British accent, while also perfectly replicating what her voice actually sounded like back in 2006, when she was 68 years old which is why I think this version of the scene is by far the absolute best version yet. I hope you enjoy this HuskyDog88, and feel free to write a review.

episodes.title: Clifford The Big Red Dog Made With Clipchamp
episodes.overview:
(credit goes to PMVUploader2, and Caio Bismark for some of the crying sounds)

A scene from the 21st episode of the sixth season of the 2000 version of Clifford the Big Red Dog, where Thomas (Jason Michas) rudely insults Jeffy's aunt Jodie (voiced by non other than, Jodi Benson), causing Jodie to sob hysterically after being insulted by Thomas This is possibly the most dramatic performance of a character voiced by Jodi Benson. Usually, when a character Jodi Benson voices cries, (like Ariel for example), the character would usually give in a few sniffles and some soft crying that is nowhere near as dramatic as this sounds, however, in this episode of Clifford the Big Red Dog, the character that Jodi Benson voices (in this case, she voices Jeffy's aunt Jodie), cries in the most hysterical, most dramatic, most heartbreaking, and loudest tone ever, and this is completely justified here in this case, as Jodie was hit hard by Thomas' insults.  

NOTE: If you'd like to know how I made that scene is I used audio of various cartoon characters, such as Pinkie Pie, Rainbow Dash, and Pearl from SpongeBob SquarePants crying (these characters were originally voiced by Andrea Libman, Ashleigh Ball, and Lori Allen respectively, however, there was an AI tool I used on a website called Weights GG, where I had a different voice model use the same crying sounds heard originally in these clips with an ai tool called voice conversion, in which case I used Ariel's voice from The Little Mermaid as a voice model and put the sounds from the clips into the model to make it sound like it was actually Jodie Benson making these same crying sounds. I also used a few crying sounds from an early rough draft of a scene from The Little Mermaid, where Jodi Benson's crying sound for Ariel sounded noticeably a little more dramatic than what it actually sounded like in the finalized cut of the film.

episodes.title: Clifford The Big Red Dog Season 8 Episode 22 Andy The Airplane Daniel Asks His Mother Tammy About Her Thoughts On The Show While The Andy The Airplane Credits Play Made
episodes.overview: A scene from the 22nd episode of the 8th season of the 2000 version of Clifford the Big Red Dog. This is an improved take on the scene with the Clifford parody of PBS called PBCS (Public Barkcasting Canine Service). NOTE: Phil Vischer (Bob the Tomato) is the announcer for the funding credits for Andy the Airplane, who is also the narrator for Andy the Airplane (which itself is a Clifford parody of Jay Jay the Jet Plane), whose voice is a slightly lower pitched version of Bob the Tomato's voice, and Caroll Spinney (Big Bird) is the PBCS announcer, with the dogs bark singing the PBS Kids jingle, and the PBS Kids Dot ident is parodied with Clifford running up to the screen in place of Dot. Special thanks and credit goes to Cmanflip and RNoob74 for the voice model of Bob the Tomato on Weights. Interestingly enough, just like the show Jay Jay the Jet Plane which used the 1999 PBS Kids Dot ident on TV broadcasts and 2002 VHS and DVD releases, this Clifford episode also uses the 1999 PBS Kids Dot ident after the season 8  funding credits.

episodes.overview: A perfected version of a scene from the 24th episode of the sixth season of the 2000 version of Clifford the Big Red Dog, where Tammy (Kathryn Beaumont) calls Cleo out for her behavior on teasing her son Daniel on being hooked on Barkydoggies (which itself is a Clifford parody of Teletubbies). Credit goes to Teletubby TV/Movie Fan 2003 for the instrumental of the Teletubbies theme. NOTE: The voice trumpet in the Clifford parody of Teletubbies, which is Barkydoggies, is also voiced by Kathryn Beaumont, and she also sings the theme song to the Clifford parody. Daniel is voiced by Daniel Radcliffe (who was most famously known as Harry Potter). Tammy also mentions in the scene that she has a whole DOGGONE BUNCH of Disney movies, (including both of the films Kathryn Beaumont appeared in, Alice in Wonderland, and Peter Pan respectively), but surprisingly, Daniel requests to watch Mary Poppins, instead of Alice in Wonderland or Peter Pan. This is basically the same video, but with the Weights ai voice model of Kathryn Beaumont that matches what her voice currently sounded like while also keeping the British accent intact.
